currentUse: Protestant church — the former St. Casimir church and school buildings at 1368 West 15th Avenue are used by the Black-majority Power and Light Church of Gary, an independent congregation led by Apostle Benny L. Dozier Sr. and Prophetess Geraldine Dozier
situation: The Diocese of Gary closed St. Casimir in 1998. The former church and school remain standing and are now used by Power and Light Church of Gary, an independent Protestant congregation.
notes: Founding year not stated. Rescue committee concluded saving the parish was impossible; bishop closed it unilaterally.

currentUse: Active Protestant church — Templo Cristiano Asambleas de Dios, a Spanish-language Assemblies of God congregation, worships in the former St. Anne building at 100 E 4th St, Spring Valley, IL 61362
situation: St. Anne closed around the late 1980s or early 1990s. Its former church remains standing and is now used by Templo Cristiano Asambleas de Dios, a Spanish-language Protestant congregation, not a Catholic parish.
notes: Last Lithuanian priest died; building sold by diocese ~1987 to a Mexican Catholic congregation.

currentUse: Church site (NW corner of W 33rd St & S Lituanica Ave, address cited as 3230 S Lituanica) redeveloped: the Lithuanian-language Draugas heritage guide says the lot now holds new housing, while the older English True Lithuania page describes an empty lot. The surviving 1908 parish school building operates as the Philip Armour public school, still bearing a "MOKYKLA ŠV. JURGIO K." plaque; it has no remaining Lithuanian connection.
situation: Bridgeport. Letter campaign to the cardinal and Pope failed. Diocese demolished the church (1990 or 1992, sources conflict).
notes: Bridgeport. Founding-year conflict: 1892 parish, 1902 building, 1909 also cited. Demolition-year conflict: 1990 vs 1992. Letter campaign to cardinal and Pope failed.

currentUse: Site redeveloped as private residential housing in Chicago's Bucktown/West Town neighborhood; the parcel at the parish's recorded address (1644 W. Wabansia Ave.) now holds a 1991-built single-family home
situation: One of the first Chicago Lithuanian churches to close; demolished without recorded resistance.
notes: One of the first Chicago Lithuanian churches to close; demolished without recorded resistance.

currentUse: Closed former combined church-and-school building (a modest two-story, residential-looking structure that held the church on the main floor and the parish school above); the True Lithuania heritage guide describes it as still standing but "now closed." No current occupant, owner, or commercial use could be verified.
situation: Our Lady of Vilna closed in 1987 and merged into St. Paul. The former combined church-and-school building remains standing, but no current occupant or use could be verified.
notes: Pilsen/Brighton Park area. Closed ~1985-1990 (1987 in Phase 1); merged with Šv. Pauliaus. Distinct from Manhattan NY Aušros Vartų.

currentUse: Probable identification: the former St. Casimir Lithuanian church building at 283 E 14th Street, Chicago Heights, IL is standing and used by a non-Catholic congregation; International Pentecostal Assemblies Ecumenical lists that address as its office (site copyright 2020), and Global True Lithuania reports a non-Catholic church operating inside a building surrounded by empty lots, with the Lithuanian name still carved in the cornerstone.
situation: No Lithuanian Šv. Kazimiero parish ever stood inside Chicago itself — the record resolves to Chicago Heights, a separate municipality south of the city. The parish there was founded 1911 (first Mass Easter 1912) and closed in the late 1980s — 1987 per Global True Lithuania, 1989 per Wolkovich Vol 3 p. 147; variance carried, not resolved (adjudicated 2026-07-27). The earlier 'Marquette Park/Brighton Park' note was a compiler's guess, likely from the Sisters of St. Casimir motherhouse there. The Draugas source articles never name a neighborhood; the ten stained-glass windows, each donated by a Lithuanian family, reached the Vilnius Archdiocese restoration trust around 2008, their maker undetermined (the Adolfas Valeška attribution is disputed in Draugas 2013-09-07). Registry Revision 1 resolves the canonical city to Chicago Heights.
notes: Marquette Park/Brighton Park area (probable). Closed pre-2013; building fate not specified; 10 stained-glass windows repatriated to Lithuania.

currentUse: Parish complex repurposed: the address 8801 S Saginaw Ave is today Casa Esperanza, a transitional housing shelter for homeless women and children run since 1994 by the Society of Helpers; per the Global True Lithuania heritage survey, the small church building itself was absorbed into the McKinley public school complex (originally built in 1953 as the parish school), which that survey describes as itself now closed. The former priest's house reportedly still stands adjacent.
situation: St. Joseph closed in 1987. The former parish campus has since been repurposed: Casa Esperanza operates at the Saginaw Avenue address, and the heritage survey records the small church as absorbed into the former parish-school complex.
notes: East Side. Second-oldest Lithuanian church in Chicago; closed 1987 as parishioners became Spanish-speaking.

currentUse: Church and school campus sold by the Archdiocese of Chicago in September 2025 to an expanding church congregation (identified as "The Chicago Church" in the Traded deal headline), which is preserving the property's use as a community/worship institution. Prior to sale it was a shuttered secondary worship site of St. Procopius Parish, used occasionally for weddings, funerals and wakes.
situation: Providence of God was canonically suppressed in 2016 after a Pilsen parish-planning process and remained an occasional worship site until 2017. The campus was sold in September 2025 to another church congregation and remains in religious/community use.
notes: 18th Street/Pilsen. Founded ~1900; closed 2016 under Renew My Church. Distinct from Detroit/Southfield RC and Scranton LNCC Dievo Apvaizdos. 2023 source tension flagged.

currentUse: Active Catholic worship site ("Holy Cross Church," 1740 W. 46th St.) of St. Oscar Romero Parish, Archdiocese of Chicago, with one Sunday Spanish-language Mass at 10:30 a.m.; the surrounding congregation is now predominantly Latino/Mexican-American.
situation: Back of the Yards. Archbishop Cupich extinguished the parish by decree Dec 10 2020; the building survives as a worship center but faces demolition threat.
notes: Back of the Yards/Town of Lake. Extinguished as a parish by Cupich decree Dec 10 2020; building survives as a worship center under demolition threat. Probable single parish (D1/D4 duplicate flagged).

currentUse: Knights of Columbus hall (307 E. Florence Street, at the Spring/Florence corner where the church was built), per Global True Lithuania's local-testimony report corroborated by directory listings placing the Oglesby Knights of Columbus at that address
situation: St. Constantine closed in the 1953 consolidation that formed Holy Family Parish. The former church site at East Florence Street is now used as a Knights of Columbus hall.
notes: Historical reference only; building may remain but identity uncertain.

currentUse: Unknown — the church at 3803 Fir Street was demolished decades ago and no source found documents the parcel's current use.
situation: Diocese closed the parish in 1989 and demolished it. Lithuanica Avenue neighborhood.
notes: Closed 1989 and demolished; Lithuanica Avenue neighborhood.

currentUse: Church demolished July 2007; per Global True Lithuania, the church footprint at 2524 Leech Ave. was replaced by a modern single-family home and only the old priest's residence remains from the parish complex (Wikipedia describes the immediate church site as an empty field). The salvaged bell-cast dome sits in storage at the State Steel yard in Sioux City.
situation: Closed 1998; demolished (year conflicted: 2001 vs 2007). Listed on the National Register of Historic Places, which gave no protection against demolition.
notes: Closed 1998; demolition-year conflict 2001 vs 2007; on National Register, which gave no protection.

currentUse: Vacant lot at the former church site (Broadview and Ridge Ave.); the parish bell is preserved and displayed at the Wyandotte County Museum in Bonner Springs, Kansas
situation: St. Casimir was in Kansas City, Kansas, not Missouri. The parish closed in a 1947 forced merger, the church was demolished, and its bell is preserved at the Wyandotte County Museum.
notes: Closed 1947 by a bishop who disliked ethnic parishes; building status unknown.

currentUse: Protestant church — Greater Generations Tabernacle, 214 Ames St, Brockton MA 02302
situation: The Archdiocese of Boston closed St. Casimir in June 2008 and merged the community into St. Michael in Avon. The former church remains standing and is now used by Greater Generations Tabernacle.
notes: Closed June 2008, merged into St. Michael Avon; favorable post-closure asset split negotiated but closure could not be prevented.

currentUse: Affordable ownership housing — the former Cambridge Lithuanian church and rectory at 424-430/432 Windsor Street were converted by Just A Start Corporation into the 14-unit Windsor Street Condominiums (completed Fall 2012, all units sold and occupied), with the Lithuanian-inscribed Virgin Mary relief preserved on the facade of the city-landmarked building.
situation: Cambridge's Lithuanian parish was real — but its name was Nekalto Prasidėjimo (Immaculate Conception), at 430-432 Windsor Street, not the 'Šv. Petro' the record long carried. That name is a conflation with the South Boston mother parish the Cambridge Lithuanians split from (adjudicated 2026-07-27; Draugas 1910-04-21: 'Naujoji parapija vadinsis Nekalto Prasidėjimo'; name correction queued upstream). The archdiocese closed the parish in 2004 and sold the property in 2007; the city-landmarked church and rectory were converted to 14 affordable ownership condominiums in 2012, with the Lithuanian facade inscription preserved as a landmark requirement.
notes: Closed (date unknown); converted to apartments with Lithuanian facade inscriptions preserved as a landmark requirement.

currentUse: Bellesini Academy — a tuition-free, independent Catholic middle school (grades 5-8, about 120 students) operating at 94 Bradford St, Lawrence, MA 01840; actively running as of its 2026 graduation ceremonies.
situation: Archdiocese closed the parish July 1 2002 and appropriated all property including a lakeside summer estate. Contrast with the LNCC parish in the same city that closed the same year and kept its own proceeds.
notes: Closed July 1 2002; archdiocese appropriated all property including a lakeside summer estate. Contrast with the LNCC parish in the same city/year.

currentUse: Site redeveloped: seven affordable owner-occupied homes (three duplexes and one single-family house) built by nonprofit Bread & Roses Housing on the former church lot on Washington Street, completed by June 2021
situation: Unnamed Lithuanian church; abandoned by 2017, razed by 2023. Only a cornerstone survives.
notes: Unnamed Lithuanian church; abandoned by 2017, razed by 2023; only a cornerstone survives.

currentUse: Private residential condominiums (reported as 15 units, including three affordable) on St. James Avenue in South Norwood; no Lithuanian signage or markers remain on the building
situation: Diocese closed the parish; building converted to an ordinary residential house. Lithuanian signs were removed.
notes: Closed; converted to an ordinary residential house; Lithuanian signs removed. Boston suburb, kept separate from Boston proper.

currentUse: Pentecostal church — the former St. Casimir's at 41 Providence St serves a charismatic Christian congregation (Church of Pentecost); the St. Casimir facade bust with Lithuanian inscription and the Lithuanian-inscribed stained glass remain in place
situation: Established 1894 for Worcester's Lithuanian and Polish Catholics; one of five Worcester parishes closed by the diocese in 2008 over parishioner objections that it was financially viable, despite a canon-law challenge and planned Vatican appeal. Merged into St. John Parish effective July 1, 2008, with the last Mass in June 2009. The church was sold in 2011 to The Church of the Pentecost; the building stands, in religious use, no longer Catholic or Lithuanian.
notes: Closed July 1 2008, merged into Šv. Jono. Solvent, debt-free, with paid-off school; financial health did not save it. Rescue committee, canon lawyer, Vatican appeal all failed. A 2010-03-09 Draugas article (corrected 2010-03-24) records this parish's ~$1M pre-closure renovation and Vytautas Ignas stained glass; post-closure the community gathered 3x/year. The former "Wooster OH" row was this same parish, misspelled — removed 2026-05-23.

currentUse: Active Roman Catholic church — Our Lady of Vilna Parish, Diocese of Worcester, now serving a Vietnamese Catholic community, with the Lithuanian interior substantially intact
situation: Transitioned to non-Lithuanian Catholic use by 2017. Interior heritage substantially preserved but Lithuanian identity lost.
notes: Transitioned to non-Lithuanian Catholic use by 2017; interior heritage substantially preserved. Distinct from Worcester Šv. Kazimiero.

currentUse: 570 Broome, a 25-story, 54-unit luxury condominium tower (completed 2019), occupies the church site.
situation: The strongest case in the record: Our Lady of Vilnius, SoHo. Cardinal Egan closed it in 2007 with no debt. NY Court of Appeals ruled against parishioners in 2011. Diocese sold the building, which was demolished. The central ownership test case.
notes: Our Lady of Vilnius, SoHo. The central ownership test case. Closed 2007 by Cardinal Egan; NY Court of Appeals ruled against parishioners 2011; building sold and demolished. Demolition-year conflict (2015 vs 2020) and sale-figure conflict flagged. No debt at closure.

currentUse: The former St. George campus at 545 Hudson Avenue houses House of Prayer and Restoration (HOPAR), a Spanish-speaking Apostolic/Pentecostal congregation; the St. George Lithuanian community itself worships at Our Lady of Lourdes Church, 150 Varinna Drive, Brighton (Rochester), NY, within the Our Lady of Lourdes & St. Anne cluster.
situation: The diocese did not close this parish. The community itself sold its own buildings during decline and moved to rented space. Parish formally still exists with monthly Lithuanian Mass; demographic attrition, not diocesan action.
notes: Diocese did NOT close the parish; the community sold its own buildings during decline and moved to rented space. Parish formally still exists with monthly Lithuanian Mass; demographic attrition, not diocesan action.

currentUse: Site is occupied by 109 Gold Street, a 7-story, 33-unit market-rate rental apartment building (units actively listed for rent on StreetEasy, Apartments.com, and Brown Harris Stevens)
situation: Demolished ~2008. So thoroughly erased that even a photograph could not be found online.
notes: Demolished ~2008; even a photograph could not be found online.

currentUse: St. George's Pro-Cathedral of the Independent Anglican Church, Canada Synod, at 1910 Falls St, Niagara Falls, NY 14303; also historically host to the Magdalene Project street-outreach ministry and its basement Rose Cafe
situation: Diocese closed the parish and sold the building to a non-Roman Anglican body, which uses it as a cathedral. Lithuanian heritage markers preserved.
notes: Closed; building sold by the diocese to a non-Roman Anglican body used as a cathedral. Lithuanian heritage markers preserved.

currentUse: Buddhist temple — the "Five World Buddhas Temple" of Guang Huan Mi Zong / World Peace and Health Organization, 262 E. Main St., Amsterdam, NY
situation: The Diocese of Albany closed St. Casimir around May 2009. The former church remains standing and is now used as the Five World Buddhas Temple.
notes: Closed ~May 2009 (Diocese of Albany); building intact as of 2019. Demographic collapse, no community to resist.

currentUse: Vacant former church complex (church, Madonna Hall, rectory) at 15-21 East 23rd Street, owned by St. John Paul II Church (RC successor parish), under an adopted city redevelopment plan and a 2025 site-plan application to demolish the entire complex for a six-story, 114-unit mixed-use building
situation: The Lithuanian parish ended in a diocesan merger. The later Syriac Catholic cathedral use ended in 2022; the former church complex now stands vacant under a redevelopment plan, with a 2025 proposal seeking demolition for a mixed-use building.
notes: Sold; became a Syrian/Assyrian Catholic cathedral. Interior retained Lithuanian details.

currentUse: Original Lithuanian church building is gone; the parish survives as Holy Trinity–Epiphany Parish, worshipping in the basement of the 1963-built parish-hall building at 207 Adams St, Newark (Ironbound), now serving a Portuguese-speaking congregation with Mass no longer offered in Lithuanian.
situation: The original Holy Trinity church was demolished after the 1981 fire, but the parish continued in its hall, merged with Epiphany in 2002, and remains active as Holy Trinity-Epiphany. Lithuanian worship has ended.
notes: Unnamed Lithuanian church; original building demolished after a 1981 fire; diocese refused repairs; congregation moved to the parish-hall basement; now Portuguese/Brazilian use.

currentUse: Active Protestant house of worship — Grace Gospel Church, a non-denominational congregation founded in Paterson in 1982, holds Sunday school (9am), Sunday worship (10am), and weekday prayer/Bible study at the former St. Casimir property on Montgomery Street.
situation: Diocese closed the 102-year-old parish March 2 2014; church and rectory sold to Grace Gospel Church (Protestant).
notes: Closed March 2 2014; church and rectory sold to Grace Gospel Church (Protestant). 102-year-old parish; first Lithuanian church 1912, current building 1961/62.

currentUse: Former church at 396 Church Street sold by the Archdiocese of Hartford after closure; interior gutted, nothing Lithuanian remains. Current occupant not verifiable from opened sources.
situation: The parish was suppressed in 2017 and worship continued at the church into the early 2020s. The building was later sold and remains standing; the purchaser and present occupant could not be verified. The Vanagas commemorative plaque was removed after closure.
notes: Closed quietly ~end of 2021, sold to a Spanish-speaking Pentecostal church. Survived review then closed. The Vanagas commemorative plaque was removed and not returned.

currentUse: Private residential condominiums — an 11-unit complex marketed as "The Gables" (The Gables at Wooster Square) at 329 Greene Street, facing Wooster Square Park, New Haven, CT 06511, with underground parking and elevator; units trade regularly on the open market.
situation: Diocese closed the parish ~2001; building sold ~2007 and converted to condos. Still apartments in 2023.
notes: Closed ~2001; building sold ~2007 and converted to condos. Still apartments in 2023.

currentUse: Home of The Abundant Life Fellowship Ministries, Inc., a non-Catholic Christian congregation (Pastor Ulysses J. Youngblood, Sr.), at 195-199 North Main Street, Ansonia, CT; Sunday service 12:30 pm
situation: St. Anthony Lithuanian parish closed after its centennial in November 2015. The church survives in non-Catholic Christian use, and the Gediminas-columns monument remains in the former churchyard.
notes: Unnamed Lithuanian church; closed and sold ~2015 to non-Catholics; Gediminas-pillars monument remains in the churchyard.

currentUse: Catholic sacred church retained by Our Lady of Mount Carmel Parish after the May 1, 2024 merger. No regular Mass schedule; weddings and funerals by arrangement, with a special Mass documented on August 2, 2026. Ancillary campus buildings were offered for sale separately from the church.
situation: Regular parish operations ended in September 2023. An archdiocesan decree merged Saint Joseph into Our Lady of Mount Carmel effective May 1, 2024, ending its separate juridic parish while retaining the church as a Catholic sacred edifice without regularly scheduled Masses. The community continues its canonical appeal and documents occasional special worship in the church.
notes: Closed Sept 30 2023 under the Hartford 2017 plan. First Lithuanian RC parish in New England (founded 1893/94). Survived the 2002 St. Patrick merger; a genuine grassroots revival did not protect it.

currentUse: Casimir Place, a 28-unit income-restricted affordable housing complex at 119 Temple Street, managed by Stewart Property Management; commemorative plaques and old photographs of the Lithuanian church remain inside
situation: Diocese closed the parish; building converted to apartments with commemorative plaques. Community noted that Greek Orthodox parishes could not be closed because they are a separate religion.
notes: Closed; converted to apartments with commemorative plaques. Community noted Greek Orthodox parishes could not be closed because they are a separate religion.

currentUse: Former community/nonprofit center (Southwest Housing Solutions' Vista Partnership); listed for sale September 2024 at $825,000 as an 11,282 sq ft office/specialty building; outcome of the listing unverified
situation: St. Anthony parish closed in 2013 and merged into Divine Providence in Southfield. Its 1923 former church remains standing but is not an active church. It was reused as a community center and was listed for sale in September 2024; the sale outcome remains unverified.
notes: Closed June 23 2013 under Together in Faith, merged into Dievo Apvaizdos Southfield. Survived a 1989 closure scare; resistance delayed but could not prevent closure. Only 34 registered parishioners at closure.

currentUse: Community center — the All Saints Neighborhood Center, home base of the nonprofit Urban Neighborhood Initiatives (UNI) at 8300 Longworth St. in Detroit's Springwells neighborhood
situation: Closed 1995 when the pastor retired; contents shipped to Lithuania. No recorded resistance.
notes: Closed 1995 when the pastor retired; contents shipped to Lithuania. Distinct from Detroit Šv. Antano and Detroit/Southfield Dievo Apvaizdos.

currentUse: Spanish-language Protestant congregation — Iglesia Cristiana Pacto de Fe Inc., listed at 5408 S 32nd St, Omaha, NE 68107, on the former St. Anthony parish property (probable; see gaps on the 5402 vs 5408 address point)
situation: St. Anthony closed and merged into Ss. Peter and Paul in 2014. The former church remains standing and is probably occupied by a Spanish-language Protestant congregation; the exact parcel match remains labeled probable.
notes: Closed/merged 2014 into Sts. Peter and Paul; sold to Spanish-speakers. Šv. Antano draugija founded 1900/01, church consecrated 1907. Survived an earlier ~2008 closure danger; ~$60K community savings deemed insufficient.

currentUse: Part of "Superior Farm," a ~3-acre urban-farm and community-hub campus at 6527 Superior Ave. owned by the food-justice nonprofit Food Strong; the 20,000 sq ft former church building stands and is slated for rehabilitation into a community gathering, event, and food-education space, with the former rectory/farmhouse becoming Food Strong's headquarters.
situation: St. George closed in 2009 and merged with Our Lady of Perpetual Help into the newly constituted St. Casimir parish. Its former church remains standing within the Superior Farm nonprofit campus and is slated for rehabilitation as a community and food-education space.
notes: Closed Oct 18 2009, merged into the new consolidated Šv. Kazimiero; old building sold by diocese, now derelict. Buyer-identity conflict flagged.

currentUse: Active Roman Catholic church — home of St. Casimir Parish (Švento Kazimiero Parapija), the Lithuanian successor parish of the Diocese of Cleveland, at 18022 Neff Rd, Cleveland, OH 44119
situation: Closed Oct 18 2009 and merged with Sv. Jurgio into the new Sv. Kazimiero parish. The former DMNP building became the worship site of the consolidated parish, which is why the building fate is repurposed rather than lost. This parish ended in that merger, exactly as Sv. Jurgio did, and the Lithuanian life that continues in the building belongs to the successor record sv-kazimiero-cleveland-oh — counting it here as well would count one community as two living parishes.
notes: Closed Oct 18 2009, merged with Šv. Jurgio into the new Šv. Kazimiero, which worships in the former DMNP building. Distinct from Detroit DMNP.

currentUse: Vacant lot with adjoining former rectory, listed for sale by the Diocese of Allentown in June 2024; a Gold Star Highway billboard memorializes the church
situation: St. George in Shenandoah, Pennsylvania, was one of the earliest Lithuanian Roman Catholic parishes in the United States and is widely remembered as the first. Organized in the late nineteenth century, it anchored the coal region's Lithuanian community until the Diocese of Allentown closed the parish in 2006 and demolished the church in 2009–2010. Its final years make it one of the record's clearest closure cases: the parish was solvent, held roughly $1 million in savings, had a credible $360,000 repair estimate, landmark status, and a community treaty, yet the diocese proceeded with demolition and took the parish savings.
notes: Closed 2006, demolished 2009/2010. Founding-year MAJOR CONFLICT: 1872, 1874, 1886, 1891 all cited; 1891 is the breakaway Šv. Jurgio parish, building 1894. The strongest thesis case: ~$1M treasury, credible $360K repair estimate, landmark status and a treaty, yet still demolished. Diocese took the ~$1M savings. Coal region.

currentUse: Private residential building; the authentic church interior reportedly remains, though the cornerstone has been removed
situation: Diocese closed the parish April 6 2008, merged into a new parish at St. John the Evangelist; later sold to a private buyer. Coal region.
notes: Closed April 6 2008, merged into a new parish at St. John the Evangelist; later sold to a private buyer. Coal region.

currentUse: Vacant lot at 416 E. South Street in the Heights section of Wilkes-Barre; a small memorial cross, likely erected by Lithuanians, stands on the empty site per Global True Lithuania's post-demolition observation. No sale of the lot, buyer, or redevelopment has been verified.
situation: Diocese demolished one of the two largest, most beautiful Lithuanian churches in the region in 2015. Site is now a flat field. Coal region.
notes: Demolished 2015; site now a flat field. One of the two largest, most beautiful churches in the region. Coal region.

currentUse: Vacant lot at the former church site on Zerbey (Zerby) Avenue, Kingston; the parish's St. Mary's Annunciation cemetery in nearby Pringle survives and still bears the name "Lithuanian" at its entrance.
situation: Diocese demolished the other of the two largest regional Lithuanian churches. Coal region.
notes: Demolished; the other of the two largest regional churches. Coal region.

currentUse: The 1903 church is gone — demolished after repeated arsons following its 1970 sale; its Latin-inscribed cornerstone survives embedded in a small warehouse-like basement-only building on the site. The former parish school on Tabor Street (which served as the worship space 1962-1993 and pastoral center until 1997) still stands; it was sold to the Sons of God church in 1997 and, per a November 2023 account, still shows remnants of the "St. Vincent De Paul" name but appears inactive as a congregation.
situation: Pittsburgh area. Built 1903; demolished pre-2017 after repeated arson. Only the cornerstone survives.
notes: Pittsburgh area. Built 1903; demolished pre-2017 after repeated arson; only the cornerstone survives. Not anthracite coal region.

currentUse: Private residential — "22nd Street Condos," 12 luxury two-story condominiums at 2132 Sarah Street, South Side Flats, Pittsburgh, PA 15203; the adjacent former St. Casimir school was converted to apartments/condos earlier (circa 2007).
situation: Diocese closed the parish in 1992 and sold the building to private developers who converted it into 12 luxury condominiums.
notes: Southern Pittsburgh. Closed 1992; converted to 12 luxury condominiums; sold by the diocese to private developers. Not anthracite coal region.

currentUse: Active Catholic church — St. Thomas More Parish, the first parish of the Personal Ordinariate of the Chair of St. Peter (former Anglicans/Episcopalians received into the Catholic Church), at 1625 N. Main Avenue / 116 Theodore Street in Scranton's Providence neighborhood; the parish also runs Maria Kaupas Academy, a hybrid classical Catholic school.
situation: St. Joseph, the Roman Catholic Theodore Street parish at the center of Scranton's early property conflict, was closed by the Diocese of Scranton on June 5, 2011. The later Lithuanian National Catholic congregation is Providence of God, a separate institution.
notes: RC. Closed ~2009 in the Allentown/Scranton sweep; building given to convert-priests. The original Lithuanian RC church Scranton Lithuanians built then lost to the bishop through the courts; precipitating event of the LNCC schism. Coal region.

currentUse: Vacant former church and rectory at 1703 Jackson Street, actively listed for commercial sale; the St. Michael the Archangel parish community (FSSP Latin Mass) that occupied it now worships at St. Lucy's Church, 949 Scranton St.
situation: The Lithuanian parish identity ended, while the St. Michael FSSP personal parish continued in the building until September 28, 2025. That congregation relocated to St. Lucy's Church; the former Lithuanian church and rectory now stand vacant and are listed for sale.
notes: RC. Closed as a Lithuanian parish; now a Latin Mass community (Priestly Fraternity of St. Peter); ethnically transferred, not formally dissolved. Coal region.

currentUse: Privately owned former church, kept largely intact as a church interior by owner Robert Damyanovich, who lives in the adjacent former rectory; not in religious or commercial use as far as sources show
situation: Diocese closed the parish ~2009 in the Allentown wave; building sold to a private individual (R. Demyanovich, ~$24,000) to prevent warehouse use. Not a community buyout. Coal region.
notes: Built 1914; closed ~2009 in the Allentown wave; building sold by the diocese to a private individual (R. Demyanovich, ~$24,000) to prevent warehouse use. Not a community buyout. Coal region.

currentUse: Vacant grassed lot on Third Street in Eynon (a village within Archbald borough), retained by the territorial successor Christ the King Parish (Diocese of Scranton) to provide improved access to the adjoining cemetery; no sale of the property has been reported.
situation: Founded 1901, rebuilt 1915; diocese closed it ~2001-2002 for mold/moisture. Demolished March 2024. A 1915 time capsule with a Lithuanian letter was discovered in the foundations. Coal region.
notes: Founded 1901 (rebuilt 1915); closed ~2001-2002 for mold/moisture; demolished March 2024. A 1915 time capsule with a Lithuanian letter was found in the foundations. Coal region.

currentUse: Church building (Sixth & Poplar Sts.) last documented in secular use as a warehouse, partly derelict with broken windows; the former Holy Cross school at 320 W. Sixth St. is a collapsed ruin slated for borough demolition; the parish community was absorbed into Divine Redeemer Parish (Diocese of Harrisburg), which remains active.
situation: Founded 1892; diocese closed it 1992; became part of Divine Redeemer Parish 1995. Home of the founding of the Sisters of St. Casimir (1907). School building tax-sold 2022. Coal region.
notes: Founded 1892; closed 1992, became part of Divine Redeemer Parish 1995. Home of the founding of the Sisters of St. Casimir (1907). School building tax-sold 2022. Coal region.

currentUse: Unknown — the church was sold after the 2008 closure (confirmed as "closed and sold" by Draugas, May 2026), but no source found identifies the buyer or the building's present occupant or use. Last visual confirmation of the building standing is an August 2015 photograph; no demolition reports were found.
situation: Diocese closed the parish in 2008 under the Allentown plan; building sold. Jonynas stained glass was rescued post-closure by the Saknys project. Coal region.
notes: Closed 2008 under the Allentown plan; building sold; Jonynas stained glass rescued post-closure by the Šaknys project. Coal region.

currentUse: Vacant former worship site; closed by the Diocese of Allentown after the final Mass on January 5, 2026, with no publicly announced sale, buyer, or reuse plan found as of July 2026
situation: St. Vincent de Paul merged into St. Charles Borromeo Parish in 2015. The Lithuanian-built church remained a worship site until its final Mass on January 5, 2026 and now stands vacant, with no announced buyer or reuse plan.
notes: Lithuanian-immigrant-built 1907; closed as a parish 2015 (merged into St. Charles Borromeo); officially closed as a worship site, final Mass Jan 5 2026. Coal region.

currentUse: Private single-family residence at 316 Pine St (Hanover section), Nanticoke, PA 18634 — a 3-bedroom, 4-bath, ~4,300 sq ft home retaining the original stained-glass windows, hardwood floors, and bell tower
situation: St. Joseph was organized in 1908 in the Hanover section of Nanticoke as a Lithuanian-Polish Catholic parish, and the surviving church was built in 1924. The Diocese of Scranton closed the parish in 2001 and joined it to Holy Spirit Parish in Mocanaqua. The former church was later converted into a private residence by an owner of Lithuanian descent; the interior was reported to remain intact. Its story belongs to the northern Pennsylvania coal-region network, where once-neighboring Lithuanian parishes met sharply different endings.
notes: Closed; converted to a private residence (Lithuanian-descent owner); interior fully intact. Coal region.

currentUse: Seventh-day Adventist church — Getsemani SDA Church, a Spanish-language congregation at 348 Smith St, owned by the Northeastern Conference of Seventh-day Adventists
situation: The only Lithuanian church in Rhode Island. Diocese closed it in 2017; building sold to Seventh-day Adventists. Community declined a diocesan offer to bring in Latin American immigrants.
notes: Closed 2017 (the only Lithuanian church in Rhode Island); building sold to Seventh-day Adventists. Community declined a diocesan offer to bring in Latin American immigrants.

currentUse: Active Roman Catholic parish church of the Archdiocese of Philadelphia; Sunday Mass in Lithuanian and English at 11:00 AM, with the Vincas Krėvė Lithuanian Sunday school operating on parish premises and a second worship site (former St. Casimir Lithuanian Church, 4th & Wharton Sts.) offering a 9:00 AM English Mass.
situation: Survived inside the diocese, confirmed Jan 2026. The only PA Lithuanian parish with a Lithuanian-language Sunday Mass. Sold the rectory ~2023-24 for $1.2M to fund operations; church deed unchanged and still diocese-owned.
notes: Survived inside the diocese, confirmed Jan 2026. The only PA Lithuanian parish with a Lithuanian-language Sunday Mass. The separately standing RECTORY was sold ~2023-24 for $1.2M to fund operations; church deed unchanged and still diocese-owned.

currentUse: Active Catholic worship site (St. Casimir Worship Site) of Saint Andrew Lithuanian Parish, Philadelphia; Sunday 9:00 AM Mass in English. The adjacent former rectory at 324 Wharton St is on the market.
situation: Survived earlier reviews then was suppressed to worship-site status July 2011. Survives as an open worship site of the merged Philadelphia parish. Lithuanian-Mass continuity after 2011 is conflicted in the sources.
notes: Suppressed to worship-site status July 2011; survives as an open worship site of the merged Philadelphia parish. Survived earlier reviews then was suppressed. Lithuanian-Mass continuity after 2011 is conflicted in the sources.

currentUse: Active Roman Catholic worship site of the merged St. John Paul II Parish (one Sunday Mass at 8:30 a.m.), with St. George Independent Catholic School operating on the same campus at 2700 E. Venango St., Port Richmond
situation: St. George remained a distinct Lithuanian parish until its July 1, 2019 merger into the present St. John Paul II Parish. The Lithuanian parish identity ended, but the church remains an active Catholic worship site with a weekly Sunday Mass and the parish school remains on the campus.
notes: Merged into an American parish ~2015-2016, losing its Lithuanian identity. Survived multiple Philadelphia reviews then was merged out. Documented only in the Philadelphia Archdiocese plan table and Key Findings (e); no full case file in the document.

currentUse: Active Catholic church — St. Peter Lithuanian Parish, 75 Flaherty Way, South Boston, operating within the South Boston Seaport Catholic Collaborative (with St. Monica); weekly Lithuanian-language Mass continues
situation: Survived inside the diocese after a ~20-year campaign; 2021-22 merger deferred. Refused merger consent Feb 2022. The community ceded the deed to the archdiocese in 1904 in exchange for a priest — the only Lithuanian church in New England.
notes: Survived inside the diocese; ~20-year campaign; 2021-22 merger deferred. Community ceded the deed to the archdiocese in 1904 in exchange for a priest. The only Lithuanian church in New England. Refused merger consent Feb 2022.

currentUse: Active Roman Catholic parish church (Archdiocese of Cincinnati), worshiping as part of the five-church St. Gabriel the Archangel Family of Parishes; Sunday Mass at 10:30am
situation: Holy Cross continues within a five-church family under a shared pastor, with a single Sunday Mass. The Lithuanian heritage identity survives in parish life and fundraising; the 2021 practice of Lithuanian readings at Mass could not be confirmed for 2026.
notes: Survived inside the diocese; debt-free; on the National Register of Historic Places (the only such Lithuanian church in the corpus). Parish dedicated 1915; survived via demonstrated vitality and congregational diversification.

currentUse: Active diocesan Catholic parish church; Lithuanian Mass Sundays 11:00 am, English Masses Sat/Sun and weekdays
situation: Consolidated parish formed Oct 25 2009 from the merger of Sv. Jurgio (1895) and DMNP (1929). Survived inside the diocese; a 2014 financial crisis was averted via a diocesan-approved school lease.
notes: Consolidated parish constituted Oct 25 2009 from the merger of Šv. Jurgio Cleveland (1895) and DMNP Cleveland (1929). Survived inside the diocese; a 2014 financial crisis averted via a diocesan-approved school lease.

currentUse: Active Roman Catholic parish church with regular Lithuanian- and English-language Masses
situation: Marquette Park. Survived inside the diocese; by 2020 the sole surviving Lithuanian RC parish in Chicago. Chronic deficit covered by the archdiocese as a high-interest loan; building valued ~$20M and not parish-owned.
notes: Marquette Park (Nativity BVM). Survived inside the diocese; by 2020 the sole surviving Lithuanian RC parish in Chicago. Chronic deficit covered by the archdiocese as a high-interest loan; building valued ~$20M and not parish-owned.

currentUse: Active Roman Catholic worship site of the merged Immaculate Conception – Five Holy Martyrs Parish (Archdiocese of Chicago), 2745 W. 44th Street, Brighton Park; regular Spanish, bilingual, and Lithuanian Masses
situation: Brighton Park (Immaculate Conception). Merged 2019 with Five Holy Martyrs into a multi-ethnic entity, but a Lithuanian RC presence and a separate Lithuanian Mass continue. Both buildings open.
notes: Brighton Park (Immaculate Conception). Merged 2019 with Five Holy Martyrs into a multi-ethnic entity; a Lithuanian RC presence and a separate Lithuanian Mass continue; both buildings open. Filed as standing/surviving.

currentUse: Active Roman Catholic parish church of the Archdiocese of Chicago, operating publicly as St. Anthony / San Antonio de Padua Parish, 1510 S. 49th Court, Cicero, IL 60804 — a predominantly Spanish-language congregation, with a Sunday-morning Lithuanian Mass still listed in Mass-time directories
situation: Survived inside the diocese; small but active. Formal Lithuanian-parish status transferred to the Mexican community in 2011, but Lithuanian Masses continued through at least Dec 2019.
notes: Survived inside the diocese; small but active. Formal Lithuanian-parish status transferred to the Mexican community 2011, but Lithuanian Masses continued through at least Dec 2019.

currentUse: Active diocesan Lithuanian Catholic parish; Lithuanian-language Masses Sundays and Fridays, English Mass Saturdays
situation: The sole surviving Lithuanian Roman Catholic parish institution in metro Detroit remains active in Southfield. It is included in Planning Area 8 of the Archdiocese of Detroit's restructuring process. The July 31 feedback window has closed; feedback review and model refinement are underway, and no final pastorate decision has been made.
notes: RC. Detroit/Southfield. Survived inside the diocese; the sole surviving Lithuanian RC parish in metro Detroit; enrolled in Families of Parishes 2025. Founded 1908 as Šv. Jurgio. Distinct from Scranton LNCC and Chicago 18th-St. Dievo Apvaizdos.

currentUse: Active Lithuanian Catholic mission of the Archdiocese of Chicago, worshipping inside the community-owned Lithuanian World Center (Pasaulio Lietuvių Centras), 14911 127th St., Lemont, IL 60439
situation: RC ethnic mission established 1990; operates inside the community-owned Pasaulio Lietuviu Centras. Survived an RMC grouping. The venue is community-owned but the mission's canonical function remains diocesan.
notes: RC ethnic mission established 1990; operates inside the community-owned Pasaulio Lietuvių Centras. Survived an RMC grouping. The venue is community-owned but the mission's canonical function remains diocesan.

currentUse: Active Roman Catholic worship site (Church of the Annunciation of the BVM, 259 North 5th Street, Brooklyn) of the merged Parish of Our Lady of Mount Carmel–Annunciation, Diocese of Brooklyn; home of New York City's weekly Lithuanian-language Sunday Mass (10:00 AM), plus Spanish (11:30 AM) and English (6:00 PM) Sunday Masses and seasonal weekday Masses.
situation: The distinct Annunciation parish merged into Our Lady of Mount Carmel–Annunciation in 2019. Its Williamsburg church remains an active worship site of the successor parish, where a weekly 10:00 a.m. Lithuanian Mass continues; Maspeth's Lithuanian Mass moved there permanently in September 2025.
notes: Williamsburg (Annunciation BVM). Diocese of Brooklyn. Survived inside the diocese; major renovation completed 2019; from Sept 2025 hosts the displaced Maspeth Lithuanian-language Masses.

currentUse: The Perry Avenue church remains open under Transfiguration–St. Stanislaus Kostka Parish, with Sunday Masses at 9:30 a.m. and 12:30 p.m. Latin. The Lithuanian Mass moved permanently to Annunciation in Williamsburg on September 1, 2025.
situation: The historical Lithuanian parish merged into Transfiguration–St. Stanislaus Kostka effective September 1, 2019. Its Perry Avenue church remains in Catholic worship under the successor parish, but Lithuanian worship moved to Annunciation in Williamsburg in 2025. The unresolved question concerns the building's longer-term use and landmark effort, not the former parish's institutional status.
notes: Queens. Diocese of Brooklyn. NOT closed: a closure letter was issued Feb 16 2025 but reversed Sept 12 2025 to limited-basis opening. Survived review then targeted. Status genuinely unresolved as of March 2026; no community buyout.

currentUse: Active Catholic worship site (one weekend Mass) of the merged St. Adalbert and Sts. Peter and Paul Parish, Archdiocese of Newark
situation: Merged canonically into the Polish parish of Saint Adalbert on July 1, 2009, the church remains standing and still holds one weekend Mass, but it is no longer an independent Lithuanian parish. Mass-time aggregators still list an 11:00 am Lithuanian Sunday Mass, and that could not be independently verified for 2026 — so Lithuanian liturgical life here is recorded as continuing inside a host parish that is no longer Lithuanian-led, never as a standing Lithuanian parish. The parish sits in the Archdiocese of Newark's 'We Are His Witnesses' restructuring discernment; no closure or further merger has been decided, so the ending stays unresolved. Church built 1895, under financial and maintenance stress by 2022 with the rectory sold after an electrical fire, and one of the last Lithuanian churches in New Jersey.
notes: Church built 1895. Under financial/maintenance stress by 2022 (rectory sold, electrical fire); status uncertain, unresolved. One of the last Lithuanian churches in New Jersey.

currentUse: Active Roman Catholic parish church — Our Lady of Sorrows, 136 Davis Ave., Kearny, NJ (Archdiocese of Newark), founded 1915 as Our Lady of Sorrows Lithuanian R.C. Church; still holding daily and Sunday Masses
situation: Our Lady of Sorrows in Kearny continues with a single English Sunday Mass; no Lithuanian Mass was found on any current schedule and the parish is absent from the Lithuanian Bishops' Conference roster. Succession (adjudicated 2026-07-27): one parish throughout — founded 1914-15 as the Kearny-Harrison Sopulingosios Dievo Motinos (Our Lady of Sorrows) Lithuanian parish, it first worshipped in St. Cecilia's parish hall in Kearny, then in a modest half-basement church in neighboring Harrison, until the present 136 Davis Ave church was built in Kearny (ground blessed August 30, 1953; completed for the 40th anniversary, 1955); the Harrison building was sold to non-Catholics.
notes: Officially Lithuanian (a Lithuanian Church sign hangs); daily Masses; by 2022 one of the strongest Lithuanian bastions in New Jersey. Survived.

currentUse: Active Roman Catholic worship site — St. George Church, 443 Park Ave., Bridgeport CT, now operated jointly with (merged into) St. Charles Borromeo Parish, serving a predominantly Spanish-speaking congregation with Masses in Spanish and English
situation: St. George in Bridgeport continues as a worship site with regular Masses, but no Lithuanian-language Mass and no Lithuanian-speaking clergy were found on the current schedule — the Lithuanian liturgical life has lapsed.
notes: Diocese of Bridgeport. Now majority Spanish-speaking but Lithuanian Masses still held; interior remains very Lithuanian. Survived/transitioned, active 2023-24.

currentUse: Archdiocesan Catholic mission with a standing church at 53 Capitol Avenue. Regular Masses ended May 30, 2026; funerals and baptisms continue. Parishioners are contesting the partial closure and advocating preservation as a Lithuanian cultural center.
situation: Holy Trinity remains an archdiocesan mission, but its regular Mass schedule ended May 30, 2026. Funerals and baptisms continue. Because the mission still exists and the partial closure is being contested, the institutional outcome remains unresolved rather than fully closed.
notes: Diocese of Hartford. The surrounding Lithuanian neighborhood was demolished by urban renewal, but the church building stands and was active as of late 2023. 2017 hall-only access flagged as transient ambiguity.

currentUse: Active Roman Catholic worship site — the sole church of Holy Family Parish (Diocese of Scranton), 574 Bennett Street, Luzerne, PA 18709; weekend and daily Masses held in the former St. Ann's (Lithuanian) church building
situation: The church at 574 Bennett Street serves today as Holy Family Church with a regular Mass schedule; no Lithuanian Mass or Lithuanian-speaking clergy remains.
notes: The one Lithuanian church remaining under Catholic ownership in the entire 10-church northern PA cluster. Survived. Coal region.

currentUse: Diocese-owned secondary church of the consolidated St. Joseph the Worker Parish, Frackville (Diocese of Allentown); regular parish Masses are held at the St. Ann site (49 North Line Street), with the Annunciation BVM church building reported as irregularly used; a chapel/youth center at 27 S Broad Mountain Ave in the old Lithuanian complex is used for Eucharistic Adoration, and the former Annunciation rectory address (7 S Broad Mountain Ave) serves as the parish office.
situation: The parish continues within St. Joseph the Worker; the current public Mass schedule carries no Lithuanian-language Mass and no Lithuanian-speaking clergy was found.
notes: Annunciation BVM. Lithuanian-community-built 1914; still open; hosted the 103rd Lietuvių Dienos festival 2017; adjacent Lithuanian museum since 1982. Survived. Coal region.

currentUse: Active Roman Catholic parish church (Archdiocese of Los Angeles) with a weekly Lithuanian-language Sunday Mass, a Lithuanian pastor, a Saturday Lithuanian heritage school, and the annual Los Angeles Lithuanian Days festival on its grounds
situation: Third building 1951, community-funded but archdiocese-titled. Active cultural center; survived inside the Archdiocese of Los Angeles, confirmed 2020.
notes: Third building 1951, community-funded but archdiocese-titled. Active cultural center; survived inside the Archdiocese of Los Angeles, confirmed 2020.

currentUse: Active Roman Catholic parish church (Diocese of Grand Rapids) with weekly Masses — but designated in the diocese's June 2025 pastoral plan for merger into the Basilica of St. Adalbert and eventual sale of the property upon the current pastor's retirement
situation: Founded ~1904; by 2024 described as the best-preserved living first-wave Lithuanian neighborhood in America. The parish remains open, but no Lithuanian Mass appears on any current schedule or bulletin, the parish is not on the Lithuanian Bishops' Conference roster for North America, and the Diocese of Grand Rapids has slated it for merger upon the pastor's retirement.
notes: Founded ~1904. Survived; by 2024 described as the best-preserved living first-wave Lithuanian neighborhood in America.

currentUse: Active Roman Catholic worship site: since May 26, 2014 it operates as the Chapel of Immaculate Conception, a chapel of St. Augustine of Hippo Parish (Diocese of Belleville), with Sunday Mass at 11:00 a.m.
situation: Founded 1895. The independent Lithuanian parish ended in 2014, when the Diocese of Belleville recorded it as a Designated Chapel under St. Augustine of Hippo Parish. Weekly Catholic worship continues in the building — a rare surviving Lithuanian-American sacred-art interior, landmark-designated — but no Lithuanian clergy or Lithuanian Mass remains.
notes: Founded 1895. Diocese of Belleville. Survived against extreme odds (11 of 13 East St. Louis Catholic churches closed); landmark-designated. Independent Lithuanian parish ended 2014, when the diocese recorded it as a Designated Chapel under St. Augustine of Hippo Parish; weekly Catholic worship continues in the building — a rare surviving Lithuanian-American sacred-art interior — but no Lithuanian clergy or Lithuanian Mass remains.

currentUse: No St. Casimir church building could be identified in Waterbury, CT — the parish as recorded could not be located in any current or historical church listing consulted
situation: Adjudicated 2026-07-28: the active/standing St. Casimir Waterbury reading is refuted. Current research distinguishes Waterbury's Roman Catholic St. Joseph parish, closed in 2023, from the historical Lithuanian National Catholic congregation founded in Waterbury in 1902 by Fr. Vincas Dilionis and carried as its own registry record. No distinct living St. Casimir parish, website, Facebook page, bulletin, or local press record was found; the relevant PNCC/LNCC research shows no surviving Waterbury congregation. This retired duplicate remains closed/lost until the underlying registry merge can be cleaned without losing source lineage.
notes: Distinct from the closed Šv. Juozapo Waterbury. Survived; still functioning 2022; temporarily storing the Frackville/Shenandoah-area Lithuanian Museum's artifacts.

currentUse: Active Catholic church — the National Shrine of St. Alphonsus Liguori, a personal parish of the Archdiocese of Baltimore administered by the Priestly Fraternity of St. Peter (FSSP) as the archdiocese's sole Traditional Latin Mass site; no Lithuanian-language Mass is offered — all three Sunday Masses Traditional Latin (verified July 2026).
situation: The Lithuanian worshipping community at St. Alphonsus ended when its Lithuanian Mass was discontinued in 2017. The building remains an active Catholic church, now the National Shrine of St. Alphonsus and an FSSP personal parish, but it has no current Lithuanian liturgy.
notes: Transitioned / de facto closed as a Lithuanian parish; building used by an American parish; one token Sunday Lithuanian Mass with no Lithuanian priest.

currentUse: Active parish church of the PNCC Central Diocese, listed under supply clergy (Rev. Thomas Basta) as of the diocese's June 2026 directory.
situation: A parish of the Polish National Catholic Church family (the historic Lithuanian National Catholic line, founded from the 1914 split), it continues with English-language Mass under supply clergy; no Lithuanian-language liturgy remains.
notes: Providence of God. LITHUANIAN NATIONAL CATHOLIC, lay-governed, independent of Rome; community-owned. The last surviving officially Lithuanian parish in the entire NE PA coal region; survives precisely because no bishop can close or sell it. Building 1915. Coal region. Distinct from Detroit/Southfield RC and Chicago 18th-St. RC Dievo Apvaizdos.

currentUse: First Haitian Baptist Church of Lawrence — an active Créole-language Baptist congregation occupying the former Lithuanian National Catholic church building at 150 Garden Street, Lawrence, MA
situation: LNCC, community-owned. Closed and sold in 2002 by the community itself at parishioners' request; proceeds went to the community's own LNCC cemetery fund. Contrast with the RC parish in the same city closed the same year, where the archdiocese appropriated all property.
notes: LITHUANIAN NATIONAL CATHOLIC, community-owned. Also called Šv. Marijos Tautinė Katalikų Parapija. Closed and sold 2002 BY THE COMMUNITY at parishioners' request; proceeds went to the community's own LNCC cemetery fund. Contrast with RC Šv. Pranciškaus Lawrence same year.

currentUse: Church site at 331 Reed Street, Pennsport, Philadelphia — long a vacant lot — has been redeveloped as a new-construction luxury townhouse ("The Enclaves" development), listed at $1,100,000 with a 2026 build year. The parish cemetery in Bensalem PA survives but is abandoned, with township/volunteer upkeep.
situation: LNCC, community-governed, never diocesan. Broke from RC in the 1916 schism; community sold the building in 1972 with ~30-40 parishioners at closure; building later demolished. Parish cemetery at Bensalem PA survives.
notes: LITHUANIAN NATIONAL CATHOLIC, community-governed, never diocesan. Broke from RC in the 1916 schism; building sold 1972 and demolished; ~30-40 parishioners at closure. Parish cemetery at Bensalem PA survives.

currentUse: A private residential home now occupies the former church lot on Main Street in Westville; the only trace on-site is the stone path that once led to the church. The parish's memory is carried by the Westville Lithuanian (National) Cemetery in south Westville, where a 2004 memorial incorporates the church's recovered bell and cornerstone.
situation: Holy Cross was an independent Lithuanian Catholic congregation, not a Roman Catholic parish of the Diocese of Peoria. The church closed in the sourced 1956-1961 window and was demolished; the older circa-1969 reading remains only as an approximate archival calculation.
notes: LITHUANIAN NATIONAL CATHOLIC, community-governed. Closed ~1969 and demolished; bell and cornerstone made into a 2004 memorial; cemetery maintained. Independence removed diocesan risk but not demographic risk.

currentUse: Active Lithuanian Evangelical Lutheran congregation worshiping as "St. John-Tėviškės Church" in the building of St. John Lutheran Church, 7214 S. Cass Ave., Darien, IL; Lithuanian-language services with Communion every Sunday 11:30 AM and Thursday 7 PM
situation: Lithuanian Evangelical Lutheran, congregationally governed, self-owned (bought its Marquette Park building in 1957). Voted to sell and relocate twice (Western Springs, then Darien Dec 2019); thriving and growing. No bishop can close or sell it.
notes: Lithuanian Evangelical Lutheran, congregationally governed, community-owned (bought its Marquette Park building in 1957). Voted to sell and relocate twice (Western Springs, then Darien Dec 2019); thriving and growing. Self-owned comparator.

currentUse: Active worship as Jerusalem Lutheran Church (LCMS), 305 Collinsville Ave — weekly Sunday service at 10:00 AM
situation: Jerusalem Lutheran Church remains active in its 1903 building as a Lutheran Church-Missouri Synod congregation. Weekly worship continues in English; no current Lithuanian-language liturgy is documented.
notes: Independent self-governing Lithuanian Lutheran congregation, founded by a knygnešys from Tauragė. Survived; small, aging, still active as of 2019. Independent of any diocese.

currentUse: Active Lithuanian parish under Quebec civil law parish-ownership
situation: A weekly noon Lithuanian Mass continues, according to the Diocese of Montréal, with a chaplain shared with Aušros Vartų. It remains one of the strongest surviving Lithuanian parish schedules in North America.
notes: CANADA - out-of-scope comparator, NOT counted in the U.S. total of 83. Quebec QC. Under Quebec civil law the parish (not the diocese) is the juridical owner; the diocese cannot act unilaterally. Survived; aging. Natural-experiment comparator.

currentUse: Active Lithuanian parish under Quebec civil law parish-ownership
situation: Two Sunday Lithuanian Masses at 9:00 and 10:30 a.m. continue, according to the Diocese of Montréal, with a chaplain shared with St. Casimir.
notes: CANADA - out-of-scope comparator, NOT counted in the U.S. total of 83. Quebec QC. Quebec parish-ownership law; diocese cannot act unilaterally. Survived; aging. Natural-experiment comparator.

currentUse: Unknown
situation: Canadian comparator. Closed October 2020 after 61 years; the community explicitly framed the closure as self-determination, contrasting it with forced U.S. diocesan closures.
notes: CANADA - out-of-scope comparator, NOT counted in the U.S. total of 83. Ontario ON. Closed October 2020 after 61 years; the community explicitly framed the closure as self-determination, contrasting it with forced U.S. diocesan closures.
